item.title: Federated Fractional Gradient Descent With Adaptive Parameter Updates for Accelerated Convergence on Heterogeneous Data
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics · Md Palash Uddin, Yong Xiang, Mahmudul Hasan, Kuo-Hui Yeh, Jine Tang, Yushu Zhang
Federated learning (FL) is a prominent machine learning (ML) framework that enables training a global model across distributed client devices without exposing their private data. However, traditional FL methods often face challenges in achieving fast convergence, particularly in heterogeneous or non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data environments. These issues arise primarily from inaccurate gradient estimation during the optimization process. To address these limitations, this article introduces an adaptive optimizer, federated fractional gradient descent with adaptive parameter updates (FedFGD-APUs). In particular, the proposed FedFGD-APU optimizer leverages fractional-order derivatives for efficient gradient computation. It employs an adaptive strategy to dynamically adjust fractional order, learning rate, and momentum to improve learning convergence and stability. We also develop a theoretical computational framework linking federated optimization with adaptive fractional derivatives, establishing the convergence of FedFGD-APU for nonconvex optimization settings with a convergence rate of $\mathcal {O}(1/T)$ . We conduct comprehensive experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and NSL-KDD datasets to validate FedFGD-APU's effectiveness under both IID and non-IID data distributions. The experimental results demonstrate that FedFGD-APU significantly improves communication speedups and testing accuracy across heterogeneous data scenarios.

item.title: Heterogeneity-Aware Federated Meta Learning for Personalized Edge Devices
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Ying Zhu, Yang Xu, Hongli Xu, Yunming Liao, Zhiwei Yao, Liusheng Huang
Recently, aided by edge computing (EC), federated meta-learning (FML) has been proposed to adequately utilize personalized data on different edge devices by incorporating meta-learning with federated learning (FL). Unlike conventional FL which conducts several stochastic gradient descent (SGD) steps to directly update the local model in each training round, FML first performs some SGDsteps to obtain a reference model and then performs a meta-step to update the local model along the direction towards the reference model. In this way, FML can identify common patterns and structures across different clients (i.e., edge devices) and quickly adapt to new data distributions, which exhibits its advantage in dealing with statistical heterogeneity inherent in FL. However, existing FML approaches struggle to effectively cope with two key challenges: i) the disparity in dataset informativeness among clients with statistically heterogeneous local data; and ii) the disparity in computing capacities among clients with heterogeneous hardware configurations. Herein, we propose a heterogeneity-aware FML framework, termed HFML, which explores adjusting the execution frequencies of SGD step and meta-step in each training round to address the above statistical and system heterogeneity challenges simultaneously. We introduce usable information (UI) as a new metric in HFML to quantify dataset informativeness, and theoretically analyze the influence of the execution frequencies of SGD steps and meta-steps on model performance and convergence speed. Based on the theoretical analysis, we develop an efficient optimization algorithm to jointly adjust the execution frequencies for different clients to handle the heterogeneity issues, which contributes to accelerating model training and enhancing personalization performance. Experimental results demonstrate that HFML can speed up training by up to 4.02× and improve model accuracy by an average of 11.5% compared to the baselines under heterogeneous settings.

item.title: Toward Model-Contrastive Federated Learning With Lightweight Privacy Preservation and Poisoning Attack Detection
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing · Hongliang Zhang, Zhongyuan Yu, Guijuan Wang, Fenghua Xu, Yongzhao Zhang, Chunqiang Hu
Federated learning (FL), a distributed computing paradigm, is vulnerable to poisoning attacks that impair model performance and privacy attacks that leak participant information. Existing FL defense schemes struggle to counter poisoning attacks under data heterogeneity and high privacy computation overhead, limiting the practicality of federated learning. To address these issues, this paper proposes a model-contrastive federated learning framework with lightweight privacy preservation and poisoning attack detection, named MCFL. Specifically, we design a novel model-contrastive term by aligning intermediate-layer representations of models in the local optimization function to promote consistency of model updates among benign participants. Additionally, we design a secure aggregation protocol that adopts two-server aggregation instead of the single server to resist poisoning attacks with lightweight privacy protection. The proposed MCFL is theoretically proven in terms of convergence, robustness, and privacy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of MCFL compared to existing FL defense schemes.

item.title: GPAFed: Gradient Projection-Guided Adaptive Aggregation Strategy for Federated Learning Under non-IID Data
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology · Xing Chang, Mohammad S. Obaidat, Xiaoping Xue, Jingxiao Ma
Under non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data conditions, static weighted aggregation strategies in Federated Learning (FL) often fail to reflect each client's effective contribution to the global objective. This limitation may induce gradient conflicts, leading to unstable convergence and model performance degradation. To address this issue, we propose a Gradient Projection-guided Adaptive aggregation strategy for Federated Learning (GPAFed). We derive a novel convergence bound that explicitly incorporates the projection of local gradients onto the global gradient, revealing its quantitative influence on global loss reduction in FL. Building on this insight, we formulate a projection-based client contribution metric and design an adaptive aggregation weighting strategy inspired by the softmax mechanism. This approach strengthens the influence of high-contribution clients while attenuating the adverse effects of low-quality updates. Finally, we provide a theoretical guarantee that the proposed strategy achieves a tighter convergence bound. Extensive experiments under diverse non-IID conditions demonstrate that GPAFed consistently outperforms strong baselines in terms of model accuracy, convergence speed, and robustness.

item.title: Correcting Representation Bias in Latency-Selected Distributed Data Streams: A Federated Learning Perspective
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering · Yibo Chen, Zhizhong Liu, Yunchuan Qin, Zhuo Tang, Keqin Li
In distributed data stream processing, buffered asynchronous aggregation collects the first returned updates into a buffer and treats them as a representative sample of the population. Under non-IID data and system heterogeneity, this latency-selected stream can be temporally fresh yet statistically unrepresentative: fast client groups may dominate the buffer while slower groups carrying complementary population directions are systematically absent. We formalize this failure mode asdirection-level representation skewand propose DirBridge, a server-side stream-summary framework that corrects the bias without delaying aggregation or storing per-client entire caches. DirBridge compresses update directions with Count Sketch features, clusters clients into spherical direction groups, and refills only the missing group mass using exponential-moving-average (EMA) group memories. The abstraction is group-based rather than identity-based, reducing auxiliary server storage. We show that group-size-aware refill can eliminate the mixture-weight error under an ideal representative condition, and we further bound the residual convergence error. Experiments on vision, character recognition, and speech workloads under synthetic and natural latency traces show that DirBridge improves stream representativeness when direction skew is large, preserves accuracy when skew is low, and incurs modest overhead. These results position direction-group memory as a practical bias-correction abstraction for latency-selected distributed data streams.

item.title: Pull-in Aggregation Protocol: A Receiver-Oriented Decentralized Federated Learning Paradigm
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Fang Shi, JianKang Zeng, Shunpu Tang, Weiwei Lin, Qiong Huang, Li Shen
Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) trains models collaboratively without a central server, but asymmetric and time-varying communication often leads to imbalanced information flow and biased aggregation. Most existing methods address this issue with push-sum normalization, which requires maintaining auxiliary normalization states and can accumulate numerical drift, thereby slowing mixing and degrading convergence under limited connectivity. To address this, we propose Pull-in protocol, a receiver-driven decentralized learning frame work for directed time-varying graphs. Instead of relying on indiscriminate broadcasting, each receiver actively pulls models from a budgeted subset of incoming neighbors and constructs a row-stochastic aggregation vector locally. This receiver-side normalization makes the model aggregation step a stable convex combination by design and avoids push-sum-type normaliza tion variables in directed model mixing. To mitigate the bias caused by directed and asymmetric aggregation, we incorporate a gradient-tracking correction mechanism. In Pull-in-GT, the model aggregation matrix is row-stochastic, while the tracking matrix is constructed to be column-stochastic, enabling average preservation of the tracking variable over directed graphs. We establish convergence guarantees under standard smooth non convex objectives and bounded stochastic noise. The resulting bound explicitly separates optimization progress from consensus induced error terms and yields the rate O(T−1/2) quantifies the mixing speed of the induced row-stochastic matrix. Extensive experiments on vision-centric decentralized learning benchmarks demonstrate that Pull-in consistently improves training stability and achieves stronger performance than representative push-sum based DFL baselines across a wide range of network asymmetries.

item.title: Joint Route Scheduling and Adaptive Data Offloading for Federated Edge Learning in STIN
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Yatong Zhang, Weixiao Meng, Shuyi Chen
In Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks (STIN), distributed Federated Edge Learning (FEL) has become mainstream methods for data processing and analysis. The traditional FEL algorithm assigns devices for local training and satellites for aggregation to perform intelligent prediction and decision-making. However, it adopts a synchronous aggregation mechanism, where model updating is performed only after all devices complete training. Considering the heterogeneous computational frequency of devices and the advanced onboard processing capabilities of satellites, satellites act as participants in collaborative local training. In this paper, we introduce a Data Offloading-enabled Federated Edge Learning (DO-FEL) framework, where devices offload part of their data to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. The LEO satellites also act as Edge Servers (ESs), while the Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellite performs global aggregation. In DO-FEL, the dynamic satellite-device visibility and the limited computational frequency of a single satellite incur additional delay for FEL in STIN. Based on this, we propose a Dynamic Route Scheduling (DRS) strategy to optimize multisatellites' assistance for the collaborative training. Meanwhile, we propose an Adaptive Joint Delay-Energy Optimization (AJDEO) strategy. For different task requirements, the AJDEO strategy adjusts the devices' offloading proportion to balance overall delay and energy consumption. Experimental results show that with the DRS strategy, the DO-FEL framework reduces satelliteside delay and further reduces the overall delay. Besides, the proposed framework with two strategies achieves the trade-off between the overall delay and energy consumption compared with other baselines. This paper provides a new perspective for efficient FEL in STIN through flexible data offloading under actual satellite-device visibility.

item.title: Data-Scarce Intelligence of Machine Learning Approaches for Agricultural Transformation in the Congo: A Review
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on AgriFood Electronics · Eloge Wabanga Kasongo, Guangjie Chen
This article discusses the potential of machine learning (ML) to provide transformative benefits to agricultural development in traditionally data-scarce contexts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Data scarcity is characterized by low-quality, insufficient, or expensive information. In this study, we review a set of ML approaches that are particularly suited to low-resource environments to address these challenges, including transfer learning, few-shot learning, federated learning, synthetic data generation, and active learning (AL). The term “data-scarce intelligence” is defined as the strategic use of ML approaches for obtaining useful insights and enabling intelligent decision-making in environments with little, low-quality, or expensive data. Key Agriculture 4.0 use cases, such as crop yield prediction and plant disease detection, illustrate the significance of these approaches. While ML systems in data-rich contexts often report accuracy levels above 90%, the results discussed here suggest that more modest but still practical performance—typically between 70% and 85%—can be achieved in early-stage, data-limited deployments. However, major obstacles persist, including very low data levels, underdeveloped digital infrastructure, and a lack of local human technological capacity. The article concludes with a roadmap suggestion for effective implementation of ML, which can lead to sustainable changes in agricultural practice and food security in the region.

item.title: FedEL++: Efficient Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Clients
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Letian Zhang, Jieming Bian, Lei Wang, Jie Xu
Federated learning (FL) allows distributed devices to collaboratively train models while preserving data privacy, but heterogeneous computation and communication resources create stragglers, slowing training and limiting scalability. Existing methods, such as client selection, asynchronous FL, and partial training, partially address this but often reduce accuracy or disrupt model consistency. We propose FedEL++, a federated elastic learning framework that addresses both computation and communication heterogeneity. FedEL++ introduces a globally coordinated sliding window, anchored to the slowest client, and optimizes block window selection across all clients under a unified runtime constraint. Within each window, elastic tensor selection accounts for computation and communication costs, while a global-aware tensor importance adjustment mitigates model drift under non-iid data. Experiments on real edge devices and large-scale simulations show that FedEL++ achieves faster convergence, lower training time, and reduced memory and energy usage, while maintaining or improving model accuracy compared to existing FL methods.

item.title: FedTADA: Trajectory-Aware Displacement Aggregation for Sparse Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Xianyao You, Tingting Wu, Hao Zhang, Wei Zhang, Siyao Cheng, Jianxing Liu
Federated Learning in Internet-of-Things networks confronts a fundamental spatio-temporal trade-off driven by statistical heterogeneity and severe client participation sparsity. Traditional optimization frameworks struggle between two suboptimal extremes: instantaneous aggregation in Drop mode, which suffers from persistent sampling variance due to tiny active client subsets, and historical caching in Stale mode, which incurs cumulative spatial divergence and staleness bias from outdated local updates. In this paper, we proposeFederated Trajectory-Aware Displacement Aggregation (FedTADA), an optimization framework formulated in cumulative displacement space. To stabilize scale normalization without stochastic feedback loops,FedTADAintroduces a zero-order probing phase that establishes an exogenous energy reference anchor. Guided by an unnormalized negative entropy regularizer, we derive a scale-equivariant exponential controller that dynamically balances instantaneous descent against historical consensus. Theoretical analysis proves thatFedTADAachieves higher-order variance suppression, accelerating the client-sampling variance decay rate from the standard$\mathcal {O}(1/T)$down to$\mathcal {O}(1/T^{2})$via a joint Lyapunov potential function that strictly neutralizes staleness bias while isolating the irreducible Local-SGD drift floor. Extensive experiments across four distinct modalities under fully trainable end-to-end convolutional architectures demonstrate thatFedTADAachieves significant accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art baselines under extreme label skew with zero additional client-side computational or communication overhead.

item.title: FuzzyCS: Adaptive Client Selection via Fuzzy Rough Approximations in Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence · Qianlong Dang, Baosheng Li, Binquan Guo, Qiqi Liu, HAN Shoufei, Guoqing Li
The client selection of federated learning presents a pivotal dilemma necessitating the harmonization of performance and efficiency. Prevailing studies frame this dilemma within the context of a multi-armed bandit optimization problem. With an expanding client base, the complexity of the task increases exponentially, demanding advanced algorithms to efficiently navigate the decision space. Fuzzy sets offer a clear depiction of the uncertainties associated with client selection, eliminating the need for intricate numerical computations. To this end, this paper proposes a fuzzy client selection (FuzzyCS) method. Specifically, we construct a fuzzy multi-criteria information matrix based on several selection criteria and use it to introduce a criteria-oriented fuzzy selection model. By leveraging the fuzzy rough approximations, we can estimate the fuzzy relationship between the criteria-oriented fuzzy concepts of each client and its likelihood of being selected. FuzzyCS can actively balance performance and efficiency by constructing an adaptive fuzzy approximation set, which incorporates the upper and lower approximate fuzzy rough sets. Experimental results demonstrate that FuzzyCS achieves the top Friedman rank in both performance and efficiency. The code is available athttps://github.com/dqlme/FuzzyCS.

item.title: FLR-SS: Accelerating Federated Large Language Model LoRA Tuning by Structural Sparsification
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Xiaoxin Su, Yipeng Zhou, Lin Zhu, Quan Z. Sheng, Ennan Zhai, Laizhong Cui
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks; however, training them from scratch requires substantial computational resources. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as an efficient fine-tuning technique that enables the adaptation of pre-trained LLMs to specific tasks with significantly reduced computational cost. In Federated Learning (FL), mobile clients operate under constrained communication and computational resources, making LoRA particularly important for efficient model adaptation. However, directly applying LoRA in FL can still incur substantial communication overhead, particularly in wireless environments. To address this, we propose a novel framework, called Federated LoRA with Structural Sparsification (FLR-SS), which reduces communication cost by sparsifying LoRA matrices through the removal of rows and columns with the smallest norms, thereby preserving the most informative components. We further provide a theoretical convergence analysis of FLR SS and formulate the selection of rows and columns as a bi convex optimization problem, which can be solved efficiently. Extensive experiments on publicly available datasets demonstrate that FLR-SS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving accuracy improvements of 1.66% to 8.63% while reducing communication traffic by 21.42% to 53.33%.

item.title: Decomposed Federated Transfer for Cross-Domain Recommendation: A Cluster-Tensor Perspective With Semantic Consistency Filtering
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering · Jianli Zhao, Qingqian Guan, Dianer Yu, Wei Wang, Jingwen Liu, Huan Huo
Cross-Domain Recommendation (CDR) effectively alleviates the data sparsity problem by transferring knowledge from source domains to target domains. To address growing data privacy concerns, Federated Learning (FL) has been incorporated into CDR, enabling multiple clients to collaborate without exposing raw data. However, most existing federated CDR methods still rely on overlapping entities to bridge different clients. Under strict privacy constraints, such correspondences are often unavailable, causing structural misalignment across isolated clients and weakening cross-domain knowledge transfer. To address this problem, we propose DFTCDR, aDecomposedFederatedTransfer framework forCross-DomainRecommendation. DFTCDR performs cluster-level structural alignment across disjoint domains through complementary modeling of transferable cluster-level structures and local residual interaction patterns. Specifically, we employ PARAFAC2-based tensor decomposition to learn transferable cluster-level structural prototypes, which act as virtual anchors for mapping isolated clients into a shared structural space. To balance transferability and personalization, DFTCDR further models local residual information through intra-domain graph propagation. In addition, a consistency-aware knowledge filtering mechanism evaluates whether each global prototype is consistent with the client local interaction semantics and retains only locally consistent prototypes to mitigate negative transfer. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that DFTCDR outperforms baselines without relying on overlapping entities. Additional experiments demonstrate its overall effectiveness and domain sparsity robustness.

item.title: DeFRiS: Silo-Cooperative IoT Applications Scheduling via Decentralized Federated Reinforcement Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems · Zhiyu Wang, Mohammad Goudarzi, Mingming Gong, Rajkumar Buyya
Next-generation Internet of Things (IoT) applications increasingly span across autonomous administrative entities, necessitating silo-cooperative scheduling to leverage diverse computational resources while preserving data privacy. However, realizing efficient cooperation faces significant challenges arising from infrastructure heterogeneity, Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (Non-IID) workload shifts, and the inherent risks of adversarial environments. Existing approaches, relying predominantly on centralized coordination or independent learning, fail to address the incompatibility of state-action spaces across heterogeneous silos and lack robustness against malicious attacks. To address these challenges, this paper proposes DeFRiS, a Decentralized Federated Reinforcement Learning framework for robust and scalable Silo-cooperative IoT application scheduling. DeFRiS integrates three synergistic innovations: (i) an action-space-agnostic policy utilizing candidate resource scoring to enable seamless knowledge transfer across heterogeneous silos; (ii) a silo-optimized local learning mechanism combining Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) with clipped policy updates to resolve sparse delayed reward challenges; and (iii) a Dual-Track Non-IID robust decentralized aggregation protocol leveraging gradient fingerprints for similarity-aware knowledge transfer and anomaly detection, and gradient tracking for optimization momentum. Extensive experiments on a distributed testbed with 20 heterogeneous silos and realistic IoT workloads demonstrate that DeFRiS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, DeFRiS reduces average response time by 6.4% and energy consumption by 7.2% compared to the best-performing baseline, while lowering tail latency risk (CVaR$_{0.95}$) by 10.4% and achieving near-zero deadline violations. Furthermore, extensive experiments reveal that DeFRiS achieves over 3 times better performance retention as the system scales and over 8 times better stability in adversarial environments compared to the best-performing baseline.

item.title: DP-HFGL: Heterogeneous Federated Graph Learning With Differential Privacy
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security · Wenbo Yu, Qingqing Ye, Xun Ran, Junxu Liu, Haibo Hu
Federated Graph Learning (FGL) has garnered increasing interest thanks to its ability to harness the representational power of graphs, while its development is still impeded by privacy issues stemming from the direct upload of a participant’s local model. In this study, we address privacy concerns of FGL by Differential Privacy (DP), and devise a novel graph-level framework for Heterogeneous Federated Graph Learning with Differential Privacy (DP-HFGL). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to investigate graph-level classification tasks in federated setting, while providing rigorous DP guarantee. The primary challenges in this work stem from the intra-client feature and structure heterogeneity among graphs, inter-client statistical heterogeneity in local distribution shifts and DP-required noise injection. Specifically, these factors bring significant variance to the model gradients, leading to unstable training and utility degradation. To address these issues, DP-HFGL applies a dual-channel model to process feature and structure information separately and shares only structural information with the server, which significantly mitigates the impact of heterogeneity under noise perturbation. To further enhance the overall performance, we perform DP operations only on the shared structure knowledge to naturally reduce the norm of local updates before clipping, making local updates adaptive to the DP operations. Extensive experiments on several types of datasets, including Molecules, Proteins, Social Networks and Computer Vision, demonstrate the effectiveness of DP-HFGL in federated graph learning.

item.title: Invariant Federated Learning for Edge Intelligence: Mitigating Heterogeneity and Asynchrony via Exit Strategy and Invariant Penalty
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Ziruo Hao, Zhenhua Cui, Tao Yang, Yunjie Fang, Xin Wu, Hui Feng
This paper presents an invariant federated learning framework for resource-constrained edge intelligence. The framework first identifies and excludes low-value or aberrant clients, and then enforces model-level invariance to preserve generalization. Motivated by pretraining-based client valuation, we show that some clients may have negligible or even detrimental contributions to global aggregation under severe heterogeneity or asynchrony. Accordingly, we propose a practical exit strategy based on client utility and delay, which removes such clients from the main training loop to protect in-distribution (ID) performance. To maintain robust performance for excluded and resource-constrained clients, we introduce FedIPG (Federated Learning with Invariant Penalty for Generalization), which promotes approximate orthogonality between invariant and heterogeneous parameter components through a gradient-based penalty. We provide theoretical analysis showing that low-value client exit can improve aggregation and that FedIPG tightens an upper bound on out-of-distribution (OOD) risk without increasing communication overhead during formal training. Extensive experiments on four domain-generalization benchmarks and multiple client scales demonstrate that the combined exit + FedIPG framework improves ID accuracy, enhances OOD generalization over recent baselines, and maintains stable convergence. Visualization results further indicate that FedIPG reduces reliance on confounding features and encourages more task-relevant feature usage.

item.title: Joint Satellite Selection and Beamforming Adaptation for Distributed Multi-Satellite Networks: A FedMRL Approach
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications · Jinsong Yu, Cunqing Hua, Lingya Liu, Pengwenlong Gu
Beamforming coordination is critical to interference mitigation in full frequency reuse (FFR) multi-satellite systems, thereby enhancing spectral efficiency. However, existing optimization-based and learning-based beamforming methods face significant challenges in satellite networks due to the rapidly changing spatiotemporal relationships and constrained on-board computational resources. In this paper, we propose a cross-task joint satellite selection and beamforming adaptation framework based on federated meta-reinforcement learning (FedMRL), with lightweight and generalizable capabilities in distributed multi-satellite networks. Specifically, a Meta-Critic network is pretrained on distributed multi-task channel state information (CSI) datasets , and then guides the satellite selection and beamforming design for new tasks by transferable meta-knowledge. An online meta-knowledge update mechanism is designed to enhance adaptability to new scenarios, which incorporates federated aggregation to continuously refine the meta-knowledge based on decentralized experiences. To further reduce the signaling overhead in the collaborative process, we integrate a dual-loss knowledge distillation (KD) module into the FedMRL framework, achieving substantial parameter reduction with minimal performance degradation. Simulation results demonstrate the superior cross-task applicability and computational efficiency of the proposed algorithm over baseline schemes.

item.title: Joint Offloading and Layer Splitting for Resource-Limited Split Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Shu Hong, Vincent W. S. Wong
The growing scale of deep models is straining learning at the edge: resource-constrained devices struggle to train locally, and heterogeneous wireless links create communication bottlenecks, resulting in stragglers. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose a multi-edge split federated learning (MESFL) framework, which facilitates split federated learning (SFL) over a mobile edge computing (MEC) system. The MEC system comprises client devices, edge servers, and a federated (fed) server. Server-side sub-model aggregation is performed on each edge server. The periodic federated aggregation is performed on the fed server. We consider a practical resource-limited scenario where all client devices and edge servers have limited computation and memory capacities. The proposed MESFL framework jointly optimizes sub-model offloading decisions, layer splitting, and federated aggregation frequency to improve the learning efficiency. We formulate a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem to minimize the learning convergence bound subject to latency and memory constraints. The problem is NP-hard, and we apply an exact finite-interval decomposition with interval-level pruning, which yields a globally optimal solution when the fixed-interval subproblems are solved to optimality, or a certified anytime solution under a time limit. Extensive experiments on the MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 datasets with ResNet-18, together with an architecture study on CIFAR-10 using VGG-11 and MobileNetV2, validate the effectiveness of the proposed MESFL framework. We compare MESFL with seven baseline methods in terms of test accuracy and training latency. We further conduct an ablation analysis to study the effects of offloading and layer splitting decisions.

item.title: Federated Quantum Learning with Adaptive Differential Privacy via Quantum Noise
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security · Atit Pokharel, Shaba Shaon, Thomas H. Morris, Dinh C. Nguyen
This paper studies a novel quantum federated learning (QFL) framework that leverages inherent quantum noise to enforce differential privacy (DP) and protect model updates from information leakage in current near-term quantum devices. Specifically, we achieve targeted DP guarantees during model training by (i) varying the number of measurement shots, and (ii) leveraging unavoidable depolarizing channel noise. To adapt privacy levels based on varying training conditions, we further introduce an adaptive DP strategy using a multi-armed bandit (MAB) agent at each quantum device, enabling dynamic control over the trade-off between privacy and model performance. Moreover, we present a rigorous convergence analysis of our proposed QFL-DP model. Our theoretical analysis and numerical evaluation reveal the following key properties: i) the global QFL-DP model converges to a bounded error floor, which indicates that, despite leveraging inherent quantum noise for DP, the model’s performance remains stable, making our approach suitable for real-world QFL applications; ii) a clear trade-off exists between privacy guarantees and model accuracy, and the adaptive MAB strategy further enhances this trade-off by enabling adaptive privacy budgeting with efficient noise allocation based on training dynamics and client needs; iii) our theoretical results are consistent with simulations, thereby demonstrating the superiority of the proposed framework over baseline approaches in terms of training accuracy, adaptive privacy preservation, and robustness against adversarial examples. Overall, the results highlight a tunable trade-off between privacy and robustness, offering an efficient and secure QFL solution for current nearterm quantum devices.

item.title: GameRLFed: Robust Federated Learning Against Evolving Backdoor Attacks via Game Theory and Deep Reinforcement Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security · Hanjie Liu, Wengang Ma, Jialin Chen, Jing Zhang, Wenbo Fang, Junjiang He
Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without directly sharing data, thereby offering effective privacy guarantees. However, the decentralized architecture of FL makes it vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where adversaries can compromise a subset of clients to inject malicious updates, causing the global model to misbehave on specific trigger inputs. The existing defenses typically rely on static rules or auxiliary validation data, which often lack adaptability against evolving attack strategies or introduce privacy risks and computational overhead. To address these challenges, we propose GameRLFed, a robust defense framework that formulates the FL security problem as a repeated game with incomplete information. Without requiring any auxiliary data, the server infers the malicious tendencies of each client based on current updates and historical observations and employs reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust the aggregation weights for mitigating backdoor effects. Moreover, attackers adaptively evolve their strategies in response to the behavior of the server to maximize the effectiveness of their attacks while minimizing the risk of detection, resulting in complex game interactions. Theoretically, we prove that GameRLFed can converge to a near-optimal global model under adversarial dynamics. Extensive experiments conducted across multiple datasets and attack types show that GameRLFed outperforms six baseline methods in terms of robustness, adaptability, and computational efficiency.

item.title: Greedy Incremental Low Rank Training ++ : A Deep Federated Learning and Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning for Softwarized Edge Intelligence
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Machine Learning in Communications and Networking · Deborsi Basu, Samriddha Sanyal, Tamal Handsa, Uttam Ghosh, Raja Datta
The paradigm shift towards Softwarized Edge Computing (SEC) and 6G networks necessitates the deployment of deep learning models as flexible, lightweight Virtual Network Functions (VNFs). However, training high-performance Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) in such resource-constrained, heterogeneous environments presents significant challenges. Existing low-rank adaptation methods often rely on static rank allocations or require heavy pre-trained backbones, limiting their applicability for training from scratch or adapting to novel edge domains. In this paper, we propose GILoRaT++, a unified framework for resource-efficient training and fine-tuning. We introduce a novelRank Demand Score, grounded in gradient sensitivity analysis, to replace global greedy heuristics. This metric allows the network to autonomously identify layer-wise capacity bottlenecks, incrementing the rank of specific layers only when their sensitivity to the loss function dictates necessity. Furthermore, we propose GILoRaFT, a Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) strategy that combines aggressive SVD-based compression with feature distillation and weight perturbation control to adapt models with minimal parameter overhead. Finally, we address the challenge of Federated Learning (FL) in heterogeneous edge environments with a case study. We propose a budget-constrained rank allocation scheme and solve the low-rank rotational ambiguity problem using Orthogonal Procrustes Alignment. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Brain Tumor MRI datasets demonstrate that GILoRAT++ achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with up to 20× parameter reduction compared to full-rank baselines, while offering superior convergence speed in federated settings.

item.title: FedLER: Incorporating LLM Embeddings for Federated Machine Remaining Useful Life Prediction
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering · Qixu Chen, Ruibing Jin, Raymond Chi-Wing Wong, Xiaoli Li, Zhenghua Chen
While numerous machine learning approaches have been proposed for machine remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, they typically rely on centralized datasets for model training. In real-world scenarios, however, obtaining these datasets is often impractical, since machine monitoring data (e.g., from aircraft engines) is proprietary to various stakeholders (e.g., airline companies) and cannot be freely shared. Federated learning (FL) offers a promising solution by enabling collaborative training of a global model without requiring direct data sharing. However, federated RUL prediction models often face performance degradation due to the decentralized and non-uniform distribution of training data. Recently, large language models (LLMs) pretrained on web-scale datasets have demonstrated strong generalization capability in representation learning, suggesting their potential to provide shared representations for mitigating data heterogeneity in federated RUL prediction. Specifically, frozen prompt embeddings provide a shared external target representation over RUL labels. This fixed representation serves as a partially ordinal regularizer that encourages compatible feature learning across clients with heterogeneous local data. In this paper, we propose FedLER, a novel framework that enhances federated RUL prediction model training by incorporating frozen LLM-derived prompt embeddings through knowledge distillation. To address the mismatch between the generic embedding space and the specific domains of clients’ local datasets, we further design an alignment module that adapts the embeddings before distillation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedLER significantly improves the performance of federated RUL prediction models under various FL scenarios.

item.title: A Comprehensive Model for Energy-Efficient and SLA-Aware Task Scheduling in the Cloud–Edge Computing Continuum
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Computing · Wassim Kribaa, Miloud Bagaa, Ibrahim Afolabi, Adlen Ksentini, Petri O. Välisuo, Mohammed Salem Elmusrati
Federated cloud–edge computing supports latency sensitive applications but complicates sustainable and SLA aware resource management. Existing schedulers usually treat energy, carbon emissions, renewable energy, battery storage, and SLA compliance separately and therefore miss the interactions among them. This paper presents a unified mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for task scheduling in federated cloud–edge systems. The formulation jointly models tier specific power profiles, renewable generation, battery charging and discharging, task migration, grid carbon emissions, and contention-aware SLA penalties. We evaluate it on workloads derived from Google Cluster Traces v3 and compare exact MILP optimization with the NSGA-II evolutionary algorithm and two greedy baselines. In the main setting, MILP produces 2.7 times fewer SLA violations than NSGA-II while using less energy, and on-site renewable supply reduces grid carbon emissions by 44.6% relative to grid-only operation. A scalability study shows that MILP suits offline planning for moderate instance sizes, whereas NSGA-II offers more predictable runtime for larger online instances.

item.title: Federated Low-rank Bayesian Approximation Learning via Stein Variational Gradient Descent
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking · Guorui Li, Ruilin Du, Ying Wang, Cong Wang, Deepak Kumar Jain
Existing particle-based Bayesian federated learning algorithms face challenges in substantial maintenance expenses in terms of computation, storage, and communication of particles, as well as the oversight of inherent correlation among particles in the lower layers of network parameters. To address the aforementioned issues, we propose a federated low-rank Bayesian approximation learning algorithm via Stein variational gradient descent (FedLoBA) in this paper. Specifically, we verify the occurrence of low-rank subspace among parameters in the same layer of particles through experiment and then design a low-rank Bayesian approximation module to decrease the maintenance costs and improve the shareability among particles. The lower and upper bounds of the discrepancy between the original and approximate posterior distributions are established theoretically. Furthermore, an aggregation refinement strategy has been developed to eliminate extra cross terms during the particle aggregation stage. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed FedLoBA algorithm exhibits superior prediction accuracy compared to other benchmark algorithms, as well as significant efficiency advantages in terms of computation, storage, and communication over its full-dimensional competitor.

item.title: Lorica: A Synergistic Fine-Tuning Framework for Advancing Personalized Adversarial Robustness
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Tianyu Qi, Lei Xue, Yufeng Zhan, Xiaobo Ma
The growing use of large pre-trained models in edge computing has made model inference on mobile clients both feasible and popular. Yet these devices remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks, threatening model robustness and security. Federated adversarial training (FAT) offers a promising solution by enhancing robustness while preserving client privacy. However, FAT often yields a generalized global model that struggles with heterogeneous client data, leading to limited personalization and significant communication overhead, while largely overlooking robustness against Byzantine adversarial clients. In this paper, we propose Lorica, a personalized synergistic adversarial training framework that delivers customized defense models through a two-phase process. In Phase 1, Lorica applies LoRA-FA for local adversarial fine-tuning, enabling personalized robustness while reducing communication by uploading only LoRA-FA parameters. In Phase 2, a forward-gating selection strategy improves benign accuracy, further refining the personalized model. This yields tailored defense models that effectively balance robustness and accuracy. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that Lorica can achieve up to 68× improvements in communication efficiency compared to state-of-the-art algorithms, while achieving up to 35.3% and 55.0% enhancements in adversarial robustness and benign accuracy, respectively.

item.title: SAFL: SWIPT-Aided Federated Deep Reinforcement Learning with Layer-Wise Aggregation in 5G and Beyond
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Haojun Huang, Hao Sun, Dapeng Oliver Wu, Juan Zhang, Geyong Min
Federated Deep Reinforcement Learning (FDRL) has been regarded as an emerging paradigm to empower various distributed Machine/Deep Learning (ML/DL) in 5G and Beyond. However, a number of approaches fail to jointly take into consideration the limitations of communication resource and energy capacity of Client Devices (CDs) to perform tasks, thereby hindering convergence and degrading overall model accuracy. Therefore, in this paper, we propose SAFL, a novel Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT)- Aided FDRL strategy with layer-wise aggregation, to realize energy/communication-efficient FL. To this end, the FL Server (FLS) adopts SWIPT to broadcast the global model to all CDs and simultaneously charges a number of resource-limited CDs for their local training. In order to balance energy/communication resource consumption and FL performance, an improved Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based Actor-Critic with Proximal Policy Optimization (AC-PPO) approach is designed to enable lightweight model uploading, by introducing entropy regularization to achieve the trade-off between action exploration and policy exploitation in DRL for layer-wise model aggregation at the FLS. Furthermore, a double-weight aggregation mechanism is designed to update the global model in an energy/communicationefficient manner. Extensive simulation experiments demonstrate that SAFL achieves optimized energy consumption and lower communication overhead without sacrificing model accuracy compared with the state-of-the-art schemes.

item.title: Accelerating Hierarchical Federated Learning under Mobility via Model Migration in Cloud-Edge-End Collaborative Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Jian Tang, Xiaoyu Xia, Ibrahim Khalil, Mengsha Kou, Minghui Liwang, Jer Shyuan Ng
Deploying hierarchical federated learning (HFL) in cloud-edge-end collaborative networks has become a mainstream approach for training models without exposing raw data. However, the non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) nature among mobile clients (MCs), compounded by their mobility, remains a structural challenge that HFL cannot circumvent, potentially preventing the global model from reaching target accuracy or substantially increasing the latency to do so. Existing solutions primarily address these challenges from the MC perspective, through implicit data or model fusion, leaving the potential of edge server (ES) collaboration largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose an HFL under mobility via model migration (HFL-M3) framework to reduce latency. Before training, it divides the MCs into class-balanced virtual sets, mitigating aggregated gradient bias and reducing the number of cloud rounds required to reach the target accuracy. During training, it dynamically maps the virtual sets to the ESs based on the MCs' current physical access states and migrates the model via the ES topology to control latency per round. Experimental results demonstrate that HFL-M3 achieves an average reduction of 12.68% in rounds and 9.73% in latency compared to benchmark frameworks across various Non-IID settings on three datasets.

item.title: Graph-Infiltrator: Unveiling Collaborative Graph Learning Risks Across Multiple Participants
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Hao Tang, Bing He, Cheng Wang
Vertical federated graph neural networks (VFGNNs) have garnered growing attention as a promising technique for intelligent network services, owing to their ability to leverage distributed graph data while preserving data privacy. For any service that prioritizes user security, backdoor attacks are a common security challenge that requires focused assessment. Unlike Euclidean data, the intricate interactions between nodes through links render gradient-based label inference ineffective, which introduces ambiguity to trigger features. As a result, existing backdoor attack strategies designed for vertical federated learning (VFL) encounter challenges when directly applied to graph data. In this study, we investigate the potential of backdoor attacks orchestrated by malicious network participants against VFGNNs. We introduce Graph-Infiltrator, a tailored backdoor attack framework, which incorporates an optional label inference strategy and sophisticated data poisoning techniques tailored for VFGNNs, complemented by a feasible model poisoning strategy. This framework facilitates malicious network participants in executing backdoor attacks against VFGNNs even when the attacker lacks label information while contending with link interference. Experiments show that with no more than 5 labeled samples, the adversary achieves attacks with success rates exceeding 90% in most settings, often reaching 100%, with negligible impact on the primary task. Our proposed approach significantly outperforms existing backdoor attack methods designed for Euclidean data against VFL, unveiling vulnerabilities in VFGNNs.

item.title: Secure Cohesive Subgraph Mining on Multilayer Graphs
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering · Zeqiang Xiao, Zhaonian Zou, Run-An Wang
Finding dense subgraphs in multilayer graphs is a key problem in graph analytics. In many real-world applications, different providers supply the layers of a multilayer graph subject to privacy policies. These providers must cooperate to detect cohesive subgraphs without revealing their sensitive inputs. This paper studies exact cohesive subgraph mining on multilayer graphs in a federated security environment using secure multi-party computation (SMPC), with the goals of minimizing costly SMPC operations and limiting sensitive data leakage. Our study focuses on the FirmCore cohesive subgraph model, which is challenging to compute using SMPC because it requires intensive interactions among providers. We propose a basic algorithm, SMPCORE, and two enhanced algorithms, SMPCORE-BP and SMPCOREAP, to exactly compute FirmCore subgraphs without revealing the providers' raw edge sets. SMPCORE-BP and SMPCOREAP balance efficiency and security by modifying SMPCORE's vertex-peeling strategy. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SMPCORE-BP and SMPCORE-AP improve performance by 1.7–7.7× and 2.4–8.2×, respectively, compared with SMPCore, while disclosing coarser-grained peeling traces.

item.title: Sketching-Based Communication-Efficient Federated Low-Rank Adaptation With Differential Privacy
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Networking · Mengyuan Zhang, Jiawei Zhang
With the rapid advancement of edge computing, federated learning (FL) has become a widely adopted paradigm for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, especially when data privacy or limited computational resources prevent centralized training. However, even parameter-efficient methods like Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) incur significant communication overhead in FL. Existing approaches to reduce this overhead, such as selectively freezing low-rank matrices, often compromise model expressiveness. To address these challenges, we propose CP-FedLoRA, a cross-layer co-designed framework spanning the model and physical layers for communication-efficient and privacy-preserving federated LoRA. CP-FedLoRA adaptively selects one of the two low-rank matrices for local training and integrates Count Sketch-based compression with AirComp aggregation to further reduce communication overhead and enhance privacy. We theoretically show that the sketching error, together with wireless channel noise, yields a closed-form privacy guarantee under zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP). We further establish a non-convex convergence bound for CP-FedLoRA and derive an optimal sketch-configuration strategy to balance privacy and model utility. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of CP-FedLoRA on both RoBERTa-base and Llama-3-8B. The results show that CP-FedLoRA consistently reduces communication overhead by 12.6%-19.9% on RoBERTa-base, while achieving comparable accuracy with over 20% reduction in communication overhead on Llama-3-8B, demonstrating its robustness across diverse model architectures and tasks.

item.title: Periodically Anchored Gradient Tracking for Over-the-Air Decentralized Federated Learning With Finite-Time Consensus
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications · Hexin Feng, Rui Wang, Erwu Liu, Wei Ni, Abbas Jamalipour
Decentralized federated learning (DFL) enables collaborative model training without central coordination. Gradient tracking (GT) improves the convergence of DFL under data heterogeneity but requires per-round connected topologies, inflating communication overhead. This paper proposes Dynamic AirComp-enabled DFL (DA-DFL), a framework integrating over-the-air computation (AirComp) on graphs with finite-time consensus. The key to DA-DFL is Periodically Anchored GT (PA-GT), which schedules additional local descent-tracking updates after the endpoint round of each consensus cycle. We derive a nonconvex convergence bound that decouples AirComp distortion from silence errors pertaining to sporadic withdrawal/absence of some users from model aggregations, revealing an irreducible error floor and yielding an approximate closed-form expression for the number of local steps. Based on the AirComp-dependent terms in the convergence bound, we minimize the per-round aggregation mean squared error via alternating optimization of the transmit and receive beamformers. Simulations demonstrate that PA-GT achieves a 25.3% relative accuracy improvement over baselines on graphs with finite-time consensus, and surpasses static connected topologies by 12.8%. DA-DFL limits accuracy degradation within 5% with beamforming at moderate SNR, and restricts performance loss to 1.4% when 20% of users are silent.

item.title: FedATMV: Towards Heterogeneous Hybrid Federated Learning via Adaptive Server-Side Training and Model Variation
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Yufan Fu, Xiaodong Lee, Sheng Sun, Themis Palpanas, Botao Peng
With the explosive growth of distributed data sources and increasing concerns over data privacy, Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for privacy-preserving, distributed model training. However, traditional FL frameworks often underutilize the computational and data resources of the central server, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios. Hybrid Federated Learning (HFL) addresses this issue by enabling collaborative training between the server and clients, but it introduces new challenges, particularly in handling server-client data heterogeneity—unbalanced, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) server data—a factor often underexplored in existing HFL studies. To tackle this, we propose FedATMV, a novel HFL framework that integrates Adaptive server-side Training (AT) and Model Variation (MV). FedATMV adaptively adjusts the server's training impact via a multifaceted scaling factor, considering server data proportion, non-IID degree, model accuracy, and recent performance trends, ensuring robust utilization of server resources and mitigating server-induced bias. Additionally, FedATMV generates diverse sub-models for clients by adaptively varying the global model, encouraging exploration of flatter regions in the loss landscape and enhancing generalization. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate FedATMV achieves relative accuracy improvements of 2.47%–31.20% over the best-performing HFL baseline across various heterogeneous settings, without incurring additional communication overhead.

item.title: Analytically Characterized Optimal Power Control for Signal-Level-Integrated Sensing, Computing, and Communication in Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications · Paul Zheng, Yao Zhu, Xiaopeng Yuan, Yulin Hu, Anke Schmeink
In next-generation wireless edge systems, efficient functionality integration is essential to address the growing demands of communication, computation, and sensing. Signal-level integrated sensing, computing, and communication (Sig-ISCC) is envisioned, where a single waveform simultaneously supports sensing, computing and communication via over-the-air computation (AirComp). Meanwhile, federated learning (FL) is widely regarded as a promising distributed machine learning framework that enables network intelligence in a privacy-preserving and secure manner, and exhibits strong synergy with AirComp, which alleviates the communication bottleneck of FL. In this paper, we study uplink Sig-ISCC design for AirComp-FL with joint target detection. We formulate the joint power and receive-scaling control problem, where edge devices’ transmitted signals should serve both sensing and AirComp purposes. The goal is to minimize the AirComp aggregation distortion subject to a joint target-detection requirement. Although the resulting problem is non-convex in the original variables, we show that it admits an equivalent convex reformulation after a suitable variable transformation. By exploiting analytical optimality properties, we develop a robust, optimal, and polynomial-time-complexity algorithm that efficiently achieves the optimal transmit powers and receive scaling factor. Simulation results validate the optimality and numerical robustness of the proposed algorithm and show its superior FL performance compared to baseline methods.

item.title: FGDPsyn: Federated Graph Synthesis with Differential Privacy
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security · Ning Wang, Yujuan Wei, Yuan Ji, Shen Su, Zhigang Wang, Yu Gu
This paper studies differentially private (DP) graph synthesis in federated settings, where each client holds a local subgraph. While existing DP graph synthesis methods assume a centralized data model, their direct deployment in federated environments suffers from severely degraded utility. To bridge this gap, we introduce FGDPsyn, a novel framework for federated DP-compliant graph synthesis. FGDPsyn treats the nodes within a client as an atomic unit and aggregates global structural statistics in a client-wise fashion. A key challenge in this setting is the linear growth of accumulated DP noise with the number of participating clients. To mitigate its impact on synthesis quality, FGDPsyn incorporates an adaptive threshold-based clipping technique that removes unreliable intersubgraph edge statistics, thereby enhancing robustness to noise. We further propose a fine-grained link construction mechanism that progressively incorporates selected edges into inter-subgraph statistical estimation until a confidence threshold is met, naturally introducing heterogeneity in edge participation across the federation. To leverage this heterogeneity, we adopt a heterogeneous-aware information extraction mechanism that fully exploits the varied edge participation characteristics, thereby achieving nearcomplete utilization of the privacy budget. Experiments demonstrate that FGDPsyn generates synthetic graphs with high utility across multiple metrics.

item.title: LeoTune : Task Offloading and Adaptive Migration for Multi-Task Federated Fine-Tuning in LEO Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing · Yan‐Ping Lv, Jingpu Duan, Xiaoxi Zhang, Jian Ma, Ke Luo, Tao Zhang
The large-scale deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites enables distributed AI tasks within satellite-terrestrial integrated networks (STIN), while federated learning (FL) has addressed the challenges of data privacy protection and communication latency of the distributed AI tasks in terrestrial networks. However, the integration of LEO satellites introduces three fundamental challenges: intermittent ground-satellite connectivity, dynamic inter-satellite topology, and limited satellites computing resources. This work introduces a LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)-based federated fine-tuning (FFT) tailored for STIN to reduce computational and communication overhead. Moreover, to optimize the utilization of computing resources and to guarantee seamless model training, we proposeLeoTune, a novel energy- and latency-efficient task offloading and migration framework for FFT tasks in STIN. It assigns the ranks for FFT tasks and jointly schedules ground-to-satellite data offloading and inter-satellite task migration. Specifically, we formulate the joint task offloading and migration problem as a mixed- integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model aimed at minimizing energy consumption and latency. To address the problem, we develop a bi-level optimization framework that decomposes the original problem into two coordinated subproblems: (i) an upper-level data offloading subproblem, solved by a multi-round learning strategy based on value ordering to adaptively select satellites; and (ii) a lower-level multi-task migration subproblem, addressed through multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO)-based migration algorithm to coordinate computation scheduling among satellites. Theoretical analysis confirms an upper bound on regret for our offloading strategy, while extensive simulations using real-world satellite trajectories and LLM-based FFT tasks demonstrate the superiority of our framework. Specifically,LeoTunenot only substantially reduces energy consumption and latency but also achieves optimal downstream task accuracy compared to all benchmark algorithms.

item.title: ISAC for AI: A Tradeoff Framework Across Data Acquisition and Transfer in Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications · Lai Jiang, Kaitao Meng, Murat Temiz, Christos Masouros
In this paper, we propose a resource allocation framework for federated learning (FL) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, where we consider not only the reliability of model transfer through communication, but also the quality of data acquisition through sensing in the first place. Unlike existing works that assume training data is pre-collected or only impose a fixed sensing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) threshold to reflect data quality, we explicitly characterize the relationship between sensing data quality (measured by sensing SNR), dataset size, and the upload reliability in FL training, and exploit this relationship to allocate resources between sensing and communication under a shared energy budget. This is non-trivial due to the intricate coupling among sensing data quality, transmission reliability, and communication resource allocation; nevertheless, it enables a principled joint optimization framework that directly enhances learning performance. Specifically, we derive a closed-form convergence upper bound that quantifies the joint impact of these factors on the FL optimality gap. Utilizing this upper bound, the original intractable optimization problem can be reformulated into a tractable resource allocation problem that jointly optimizes the sensing transmit power, number of sensing snapshots, and communication transmit power at each device subject to individual energy budget constraints. To solve the reformulated problem, we propose a two-layer optimization algorithm with linear complexity, where the outer layer employs golden section search and the inner layer solves per-device subproblems with closed-form solutions.

item.title: Optimizing Value of Learning in Task-Oriented Federated Meta-Learning System Over NOMA Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications · Bibo Wu, Fang Fang, Xianbin Wang
A key limitation of federated learning (FL) is that its one-size-fits-all global model fails to provide customized solutions for the diverse tasks encountered in modern edge networks. Federated meta-learning (FML) offers a promising remedy by allowing each device to fine-tune the local model. However, the performance of FML can still be constrained by heterogeneous task requirements and resource costs, as well as limited communication efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose a task-oriented FML framework over non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) cluster-based networks. A novel metric, termed value of learning (VoL), is proposed to quantify the training utility of devices. Additionally, to prioritize the task of each device, a task-level weight (TLW) metric is defined. We aim to maximize the sum of TLW-based VoL across all devices. The formulated problem is non-convex. To solve it, we first analyze the two-device cluster case, where the problem is effectively solved using problem decomposition and convex optimization techniques. For the more complex case involving multiple devices per cluster, we develop a parameterized deep Q-network (PDQN)-based reinforcement learning algorithm to jointly optimize discrete and continuous variables. Simulation results for both scenarios demonstrate that the proposed approaches significantly outperform benchmark schemes, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed solutions in enhancing FML performance.

item.title: FedDTE-IDS: A Federated Dual-Model Deep Transfer Ensemble Framework for Privacy-Preserving Advanced Persistent Threat Detection in Heterogeneous Industrial Internet of Things Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems · Singmaneni Krishnapriya, Sukhvinder Singh, Amaravarapu Pramodkumar
Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) against multi-site industrial control networks are rare and camouflaged: on CICAPT-IIoT fewer than one flow in 9,000 is malicious. Sites cannot pool raw traffic under IEC 62443 and GDPR, and federated learning with differential privacy (DP) adds noise scaled to the whole model update, which at this imbalance can erase the attack-class gradient. This paper addresses one problem: keeping attack-class recall above a stated floor while federated training across heterogeneous industrial sites carries an explicit$(\epsilon,\delta)$-DP guarantee. FedDTE-IDS places the DTE-IDS dual-backbone detector at the OT/IT boundary of each site and trains it with three mechanisms: FedHDH, client-side SMOTE in image-pixel space; PAFA, which fixes a recall floor and selects the largest admissible noise multiplier, reversing the usual fix-$\epsilon$search; and DFCA, which weights client updates by attack-class F1 on a server-held calibration set. On CICAPT-IIoT partitioned into five non-IID clients, FedDTE-IDS reaches recall 93.03%, F1 80.78% and PR-AUC 0.8941 under client-level$(\epsilon {=}43.3,\ \delta {=}10^{-5})$-DP with Rényi accounting, 1.99 recall points below the non-private centralised baseline (not statistically significant on 201 attack flows) and 6.47 points above DP-FedAvg at the same noise level (Holm-corrected$p{< }0.004$). Poisoning, heterogeneity, and label-free cross-domain evaluations are also reported.

item.title: Hybrid Field Wireless Federated Diffusion Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications · Tianci Wang, Jie Zheng, Lvhang Wen, Hongyang Du, Jiawen Kang, Jie Ren
Deploying extra-large reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (XL-RIS) is essential to assist over-the-air federated learning (AirFL) for 6G edge intelligence. However, this massive infrastructure inherently induces high-dimensional hybrid-field channels, constraining system performance alongside the computational challenges of joint communication-learning optimization for generative AI models. In this paper, we propose a hybrid-field communication-learning joint optimization framework using graph neural networks (GNNs) for XL-RIS-assisted over-the-air federated diffusion learning (AirFDL). Diffusion models are integrated into local training to correct gradient deviations from hybrid-field channel distortions, enhancing global model robustness. We develop a hybrid-field XL-RIS channel model that unifies spherical-wave near-field and plane-wave far-field propagation. To mitigate gradient aggregation limitations from weak links, we design a permutation-equivariant GNN-based joint optimization algorithm. By representing users, RIS elements, and the server as a dynamic heterogeneous graph, our method leverages message passing to learn the relationship between channel states, RIS phase shifts, and transmit power, reducing computational complexity of beamforming and resource allocation. Furthermore, a 1-bit momentum-sign gradient compression is incorporated to fundamentally minimize communication overhead while ensuring training stability against hybrid-field impairments. Simulation results demonstrate that AirFDL improves wireless FL efficiency through diffusion-driven denoising, effectively preserving aggregation performance.

item.title: Secure and Efficient Model Aggregation for Resilient Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security · Mengqian Li, Youliang Tian, Junpeng Zhang, Ruixin Song, Ze Yang, Jinbo Xiong
Federated learning (FL) has received considerable attention for its distributed collaborative training properties, which can construct the global model without sharing private datasets of clients scenarios. In order to overcome data silos, clients individually train models on local data and share the model parameters with the server for global aggregation. In this paper, we propose a secure and efficient aggregation FL framework, namely FedSEA, which provides lightweight protection for clients’ local models, while allowing accurate aggregation of the protected coefficients. Specifically, the server applies truncated SVD to the initial global model and distributes the quantized retained bases to clients for local caching. Each client reuses these bases to project its residual-compensated local model and uploads only quantized pseudo-singular values rather than computing a local SVD or transmitting low-rank factors. The local residual preserves discarded information without increasing the transmitted payload. Moreover, FedSEA employs a pairwise and server-client symmetric masking noise, which is implemented through Diffie–Hellman-based shared key exchange and pseudo-random generator. The masks are removed exactly during coefficient aggregation, after which the server reconstructs the aggregated model. When selected clients drop out, FedSEA removes their residual masks and aggregates the remaining active clients, thereby preserving system resilience. Extensive theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of FedSEA in improving communication efficiency while preserving model utility and security.

item.title: TAFL: Trust-Aware Federated Learning for Anomalous Client Detection, Isolation, and Recovery
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security · Md Mamunur Rashid, Md Palash Uddin, Yong Xiang, Keshav Sood, Yushu Zhang, Longxiang Gao
Federated Learning (FL) systems remain vulnerable to anomalous clients, including unreliable participants and malicious adversaries. Such clients can manipulate updates, poison data, exhibit non-IID drift, or participate intermittently, degrading model integrity, convergence, and trust. To address this, we propose Trust-Aware Federated Learning (TAFL), a unified framework for anomalous-client detection, probationary isolation, and controlled reintegration. TAFL combines Subjective Logic (SL) and Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) to provide uncertainty-aware trust estimation and peer-informed stabilization under dynamic participation. Targeting adaptive adversaries under bounded compromise capabilities, TAFL applies multi-signal consistency screening, including behavioral consistency and attribution drift, to detect subtle deviations beyond obvious outliers. Low-trust clients enter probationary isolation and are reintegrated only after sustained behavioral recovery. To promote fairness and deter malicious participation, TAFL enforces trust- and quality-aligned incentives with auditable smart-contract enforcement and provides theoretical analysis supporting convergence, trust recovery, and bounded adversarial influence. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR10 show 2–4% higher anomalous-client detection and 20–25% lower convergence latency under 10–30% anomalous-client ratios. FEMNIST results further confirm robustness under stronger user-level heterogeneity, while stress tests on CIFAR10 show 94.6–97.1% mean detection and reduce semantic-backdoor attack success rate (ASR) to 2.9%.

item.title: Label-Aware Distribution-Based Dynamic Weighting Aggregation for Hierarchical Backdoor Defense in Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security · Xi Chen, Chunyi Zhou, Rui Zeng, Xiaogang Xu, Jianmin Wu, Zhe Liu
Federated learning (FL) is vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where malicious clients inject poisoned updates into the global model through local training. Existing defenses mainly rely on anomaly detection, yet their effectiveness is often undermined by non-IID data distributions and the subtle similarity between benign and malicious updates. To address these challenges, we proposeLabel-Aware Distribution-based Dynamic Weighting (LADW), a novel black-box aggregation strategy that operates without any trusted client information. Leveraging a small auxiliary dataset, even one consisting of synthetic data generated by a large text-to-image model, LADW infers each client’s implicit label distribution from update similarity and dynamically adjusts aggregation weights to suppress label-concentrated, potentially malicious updates. Furthermore, LADW can be seamlessly integrated with existing detection-based defenses, forming an adaptive and hierarchical framework that combines detection, norm clipping, and dynamic aggregation, while also enabling inference of the adversary’s target label. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that LADW substantially enhances the effectiveness of existing defenses by reducing attack success rates while improving the global model’s main-task accuracy. Notably, under highly non-IID conditions, LADW achieves state-of-the-art performance, highlighting its robustness and adaptability across diverse federated learning settings.
